name: בַּעַל זְבוּב
summary: The god of Ekron whom Ahaziah king of Israel sent to inquire of when he fell sick; Elijah met the messengers: “Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are going to inquire of Baal-zebub the god of Ekron?”, and Ahaziah died as Yahweh said (2Ki 1:2–17). The name is בַּעַל “lord” with זְבוּב “fly” (Ecc 10:1; Isa 7:18), “lord of flies”. In the gospels Βεελζεβούλ is the name the scribes and Pharisees gave to the ruler of the demons, saying Jesus cast out demons by him; Jesus answered that he cast them out by the spirit (finger) of God, and that a kingdom divided against itself cannot stand (Mat 12:24–28; Luk 11:15–20).

evidence.note: “Go, inquire of בַּעַל זְבוּב the god of Ekron, whether I shall recover.”
“Is it because there is no God in Israel?”
“You shall surely die.” So he died, according to the word of Yahweh.
“Dead flies (זְבוּבֵי מָוֶת) make the perfumer's oil stink”: זְבוּב “fly”.
“If they called the master of the house Βεελζεβούλ, how much more those of his household.”
“This man casts out demons only by Βεελζεβούλ”; “if I by the spirit of God cast out demons, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.”
“If I by the finger of God cast out demons.”
From Hebrew בַּעַל “lord”; the form Beelzebub comes through the Vulgate from 2Ki 1:2, בַּעַל זְבוּב, “lord of flies”.

note: TIPNR keys Baal-zebub@2Ki.1.2 as a person (Male). No bdb key: Strong's 1176 is filed under b.ci.ab in the database, the root entry noun's key, and a key belongs to one entry only. The gospels' Βεελζεβούλ (-ούλ, not -ούβ) is perhaps a play on זְבֻל “habitation” (cf. Mat 10:25 οἰκοδεσπότης) or on later Aramaic זֶבֶל “dung”; not decided. The gospel passages report what Jesus' opponents said; the name is not given a meaning of its own there.
